title: Alcohol Was Originally the Name of an Eye Makeup Powder
hook: Alcohol comes from the name of a black powder worn around the eyes

open.title: The word alcohol has eye makeup hiding inside it
open.line: The word alcohol comes from Arabic. But the first thing it named wasn't something you drink.

summary: Alcohol comes from al-kuhl, Arabic for eye makeup powder. The word for fine powder widened to distilled substances, then narrowed to ethanol, the ingredient in drinks.

text: Long ago people kept black powder in pots like this and applied it around their eyes.
It's kohl, a cosmetic Egyptians had used since around 3100 BC.
Kohl was traditionally made by grinding a mineral called stibnite.
In Arabic, this powder is called al-kuhl.

panels.text: What does that have to do with booze?

text: Al is the Arabic article, like the in English.
At first it named a very fine stibnite powder.
People thought of it as the essence of that mineral.
A 1543 English translation calls alcohol the finest powder.
Every substance obtained by distilling became alcohol.
Actually, it narrowed again after that.
Of all distilled things, ethanol, the ingredient in drinks, became what alcohol means.
A name for eye powder went the long way round and now sits on bottle labels.
